draft.title: The sine rule
card: In triangle ABC, side \(a\) is opposite angle \(A\), side \(b\) is opposite angle \(B\), and side \(c\) is opposite angle \(C\).
The sine rule says \(\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C}\). Each side divided by the sine of its opposite angle gives the same value.
Use it when you know a side and its opposite angle, plus one more side or angle. To find a side, put the unknown side on top: \(\frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{a}{\sin A}\).
draft.remember: Match each side with the sine of the angle opposite it.

a.q: In triangle PQR, \(p = 7\) cm, \(P = 35^{\circ}\) and \(Q = 62^{\circ}\). Which line gives the length of \(q\)?
a.why: Side \(p\) is opposite \(P\) and side \(q\) is opposite \(Q\), so \(\frac{q}{\sin 62^{\circ}} = \frac{7}{\sin 35^{\circ}}\). Multiplying both sides by \(\sin 62^{\circ}\) gives the first option. The second option swaps the two angles.
a.clue: Write the rule with \(q\) on top, then multiply both sides.

b.q: Tom surveys a triangular paddock. One side is 120 m and is opposite an angle of \(50^{\circ}\). The side \(x\) is opposite an angle of \(70^{\circ}\). How long is \(x\), to the nearest 0.1 m?
b.why: \(\frac{x}{\sin 70^{\circ}} = \frac{120}{\sin 50^{\circ}}\), so \(x = \frac{120 \sin 70^{\circ}}{\sin 50^{\circ}} \approx 147.2\) m. Putting \(\sin 50^{\circ}\) on top gives 97.8 m, which pairs each side with the wrong angle.
b.clue: The larger angle is opposite the longer side.

wants.brief: A triangle ABC with vertices labelled A, B and C. The side opposite A is labelled a, the side opposite B is labelled b, and the side opposite C is labelled c. Each angle is marked at its vertex.
wants.why: It shows which side is opposite which angle.

problems.detail: Why (a) names options by position ('gives the first option', 'the second option swaps the two angles'), but the options are shuffled. As shown, the first option is the product 7 sin 35° × sin 62°, which is wrong, and the swapped-angle option is the third, not the second. The why should name the option by its content, e.g. q = 7 sin 62° / sin 35°.

check.summary: The card, the worked example and both answers are correct (q = 7 sin 62°/sin 35°; x ≈ 147.2 m). The only problem is that why (a) refers to options by position ('first', 'second'), which does not match the displayed order and would point students to a wrong option.
